_README: The DEMO copy of sos_fade_demo (SOS Fade), made 2026-09-11 so the same strategy trades the demo account in its own process while the original trades the live one. Aaron's call: a demo copy can be moved onto a NEW version to trial it while live keeps the proven one, which one signal sent to two accounts could never do. So the two are DELIBERATELY independent - a promote of one does not move the other, and a setting changed in one file is not changed in the other. Every strategy setting below was copied from sos_fade_demo's config on 2026-09-11, when the live bot was running the snapshot built from 3483e40e; WHY each holds its value is written in that file, not repeated here, because a second copy of those notes would be a second answer. Which account it trades is the account field, set from Bots -> Accounts; null BENCHES it (the boot sequence and the watchdogs skip it, the runner refuses it). It was born benched so the box could deploy its snapshot BEFORE anything expected it to run: the watchdog starts an assigned bot it finds down within a minute, and without a snapshot that start would fail every minute. No secrets live here: the MT5 password is in algos/credentials.json under mt5_accounts.
_display_name: The strategy's name and nothing about where it runs, the same as the original's (2026-09-11). It said 'SOS Fade (demo)' for a day, which would have gone on saying demo on real money the moment this bot was moved. What tells the two copies apart in Telegram is the account's kind, added to every message as LIVE or demo when it is sent (bot_state.labelled), and live accounts' trades and signals go to their own channels (algos/shared/telegram_rooms.json).
_mt5_path: The MT5_FFT terminal, which serves the demo account 700152905 in accounts.json. A placeholder while benched: assigning the bot to an account ADOPTS that account's terminal, server and symbol suffix.
_magic: 770125 = the original's 770115 plus 10, so the last digit still names the strategy in the terminal's order list. live_config._assert_magic_is_unique only refuses a clash on ONE account and the original trades another, so sharing would have been legal - it is distinct anyway because sos_fade_demo traded account 700152905 under 770115 until 2026-09-11, and a copy reading those deals back as its own is the doubled-book failure the magic exists to prevent.
_sizing_basis_adjustment: 0: this bot sizes off the balance it finds. The -4518.23 once held by sos_fade_demo was measured on this demo account and described THAT bot's own equity path (the 2026-08-25 duplicate fills and the 2026-08-26 oversized short); a fresh bot inherits none of it. Compare this copy with the live one in R, never in dollars - the two accounts' balances are nothing alike.
